completion_conditions: The MergeGate metadata job reads every page of the Guardian evidence feeds.
An empty head SHA can never satisfy the head binding.
A comment that merely contains the head SHA somewhere does not satisfy the head binding; the canonical position does.
The bot only ever overwrites its own status comment.
The full suite, the guardian-policy, evidence-integrity, governance-evidence, adversarial, control-plane, init, workflow-lint and shellcheck suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: DEFECT 1 (fail-open, live). `.github/workflows/shiki-mergegate.yml` lines 63, 64, 65 fetch the Guardian comments, events and timeline feeds WITHOUT `--paginate`, while `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml` lines 96, 97, 98 all carry it. The un-paginated job is the MergeGate metadata check — the job that gates Contract PRs — so once a PR exceeds one page of comments the Guardian approval is simply not in the evidence the gate reads. It fails open in the other direction too: a NEGATION comment past page one is equally invisible, so a revoked approval still passes.

DEFECT 2 (fail-open, exploitable). `scripts/shiki_guardian.py:385` tests `if policy.require_head_sha and head_sha not in body`. With `head_sha` empty, `'' not in body` is False for every body, so the guard never fires and a marker comment naming ANY SHA — or none — counts as a current-head approval.

DEFECT 3 (fail-open, narrower). The same line is a substring test over the WHOLE body. A body that merely quotes the head SHA — a Guardian quoting the bot's own status comment, which renders the full SHA — satisfies the head binding without anyone intending to approve. The canonical body is produced by `build_approval_body(marker, head_sha)` in `scripts/shiki_guardian_status.py`, so a positional check is available.

DEFECT 4 (write-side). `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml:282` selects the comment to PATCH with `map(select((.body // "") | contains("<!-- shiki:guardian-status -->"))) | (.[0].id // empty)` — no author predicate. The first comment containing that marker wins regardless of author, so a human who quotes the marker gets overwritten by the bot.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-04, the step whose absence blocked three tasks). Tightening the body shape in defect 3 makes the loose prose form illegal, and FIVE files outside the originally-drafted locks hold approving fixtures in that form: `tests/test_guardian_evidence.py` (its `test_line_initial_marker_approves` is a NAMED assertion that the loose form approves — the behaviour this task makes illegal), `tests/test_contract_open.py`, `tests/test_contract_plan_registration.py`, `scripts/test_shiki_evidence_integrity.sh` and `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh`. All five are MUST-CHANGE and are in the locks.

`docs/agents/guardian-policy.md` is also in the locks: after defect 3 the whole body shape is load-bearing, and the document currently instructs the Guardian to use the marker alone. `validate_shiki.py:777-785` requires its listed needles to be PRESENT, so adding prose is safe and removing any listed needle is fatal — the task must add, never replace.
`tests/test_workflow_invocation.py` is NOT affected and is deliberately excluded: `_mergegate_invocation` slices from the `scripts/mergegate_check.py` token onward, and this task adds no CLI flag.

MUST-NOT-BREAK, verified: the `|| echo "[]"` fallbacks at `shiki-mergegate.yml:63-65` encode 'a fetch failure is a deterministic no-approval' (comment at :58-62) and must survive verbatim; `scripts/validate_shiki.py:750-765` pins the exact `--guardian-policy`, `--guardian-comments`, `--guardian-events` argument strings; `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh`, `scripts/test_shiki_init.sh`, `scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh --strict` and `scripts/test_shiki_shellcheck.sh --strict` all gate this change and are in the verification command, not the locks.

Fixing defect 3 by requiring the canonical position is a behaviour change for anyone approving in free-form prose. That is deliberate: the approval body is machine-generated by `shiki guardian status --format comment` and pasted, and a positional rule makes 'the Guardian meant to approve THIS head' provable rather than inferred.

The four are one task. They share one evidence surface, and splitting them would mean four PRs each re-proving the same fixture shapes. One independent test per defect is required, so a partial fix cannot pass.

outcome: The Guardian approval gate can no longer be satisfied by evidence it never read, by a substring that happens to appear anywhere in a comment, or by an empty head SHA; and the bot can no longer overwrite a human's comment. Three of the four are fail-open — the gate says approved when it should not — and all four were found by adversarially attacking the approval surface, not by any test.

tasks.scope:
Fix four defects in one change; each needs its own test and none may be dropped.

1. PAGINATION. Add `--paginate` to all three `gh api` calls that build `.shiki/gha/live-guardian-comments.json`, `live-guardian-events.json` and `live-guardian-timeline.json` in `.github/workflows/shiki-mergegate.yml`, matching `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml`. Keep the existing `|| echo "[]"` fallbacks EXACTLY as they are — they encode 'a fetch failure is a deterministic no-approval'. Add a control-plane assertion that every Guardian-evidence `gh api` call in BOTH workflows carries `--paginate`, so the two cannot drift apart again.

2. EMPTY HEAD SHA. In `scripts/shiki_guardian.py` `_comment_source`, the condition at line 385 must not pass vacuously when `head_sha` is empty. An empty head SHA with `require_head_sha` set is MISSING evidence, so it must produce the SAME soft blocker a stale comment produces — never silent acceptance.

3. POSITIONAL HEAD BINDING. Replace the whole-body substring test with a positional one: the body must contain exactly one 40-character hex token, and it must equal `head_sha`, in the shape `build_approval_body` (`scripts/shiki_guardian_status.py`) produces. Zero tokens, two or more tokens, or an abbreviated SHA is a soft blocker naming what was wrong. Keep the marker, negation-marker and actor checks in their current ORDER — extraction must happen after `_configured_guardian` and `_author_allowed`, so a comment from a non-Guardian is never even parsed for a SHA.

4. PATCH TARGET. In `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml`, the jq filter that picks the guardian-status comment to update must also select on author: only a comment written by `github-actions[bot]` may be PATCHed. When no bot comment exists, post a new one as it does today.

FIXTURE MIGRATION (this is why the locks are wider than the code being fixed). Defect 3 makes the loose prose approval form illegal, and five files hold approving fixtures in that form: `tests/test_guardian_evidence.py` — including `test_line_initial_marker_approves`, a NAMED assertion that the loose form approves, which must become an assertion that it does NOT; `tests/test_contract_open.py`; `tests/test_contract_plan_registration.py`; `scripts/test_shiki_evidence_integrity.sh`; `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh`. Canonicalize each approving fixture to the `build_approval_body` shape. Do not weaken any assertion to make it pass — where a fixture proves approval, it must still prove approval, through the canonical body.

Document the tightened body shape in `docs/agents/guardian-policy.md` by ADDING prose. Never remove or reword an existing needle: `validate_shiki.py:777-785` requires the listed strings to be present and their absence is fatal.

Add `tests/test_guardian_approval_binding.py` driving `evaluate_guardian_approval` and `_comment_source` directly, with at least one case per defect and a negative assertion that the Guardian requirement still resolves as REQUIRED in every rejecting case: head_sha='' with a well-formed marker comment is NOT approved; head_sha='' with no comment is NOT approved; a body quoting the head SHA inside other prose is NOT approved; a body with two 40-hex tokens is NOT approved; an abbreviated SHA is NOT approved; the canonical `build_approval_body` output IS approved; a marker comment from a non-configured actor is rejected at the actor check and never parsed — assert the ORDERING, not only the outcome; a negation comment still blocks.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Defect 1 measured: `grep -c -- '--paginate' .github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml` → 6; the same grep against `.github/workflows/shiki-mergegate.yml` → 0. GitHub's issue-comments API pages at 30 by default, so on a PR with more than 30 comments the job that gates Contract PRs cannot see an approval posted later than the 30th comment — and cannot see a REVOCATION either.
  Defect 2 measured by reading `_comment_source`: `if policy.require_head_sha and head_sha not in body`. Python evaluates `'' not in body` as False for every string, so with an empty head SHA the guard is dead and any marker comment from a configured Guardian is accepted as current-head.
  Defect 3, same line: `in` is a substring test over the entire body, and the bot's own status comment renders the full head SHA, so a Guardian quoting it — a normal thing to do when explaining a blocker — would satisfy the binding without approving.
  Defect 4 measured at `shiki-cca-completion.yml:282`: the jq filter selects `.[0]` of every comment containing the guardian-status marker with no author predicate, so the bot PATCHes whichever appears first — including a human's.
  How these were found: not by any test, but by adversarially attacking the approval surface while designing the base-sync approval carry. That is the durable lesson — the approval path had no adversarial test of its own evidence handling.
  Why the locks are 12 and not 6: the lock-sufficiency audit found five fixture holders outside the obvious set, all made illegal by defect 3. Three tasks were blocked earlier the same week by exactly this omission.
  Reproducible when: each of the four cases is rejected or corrected, every rejection still leaves the Guardian requirement resolving as required, and all eight gating suites stay green.
